benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, adjusted from MLIT transactions via Utinokati and 2026 official points: Maebashi ~16 (NOT the 28.2 all-use average, which is commercial, and NOT the 59.2 Honmachi top commercial point), Shin-Maebashi ~17, Chuo-Maebashi ~18 (official-points proxy), Mitsumata ~15 (NOT the 18.8 figure, which rests on exactly one official point), Joto ~16 (proxy), Katagai ~14 (proxy), Maebashi-Oshima ~14 in-zone, Gunma-Soja ~12, Ogo ~6, Higokoshi ~5 and Araya ~5 (low-confidence proxies). Urbanisation-control and non-line-drawn (非線引き) land is scored only against its own comparables, with zoning and rebuild status printed on the card. Walk bands are nearly flat — the official-point ladder implies only about −10–15% by a 30-minute walk: Maebashi is a car market (average transacted walk 29 minutes for houses and land alike), so walk distance is weighted gently on this page. Used houses transacted at about ¥57万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis): the station / Minami-cho / Bunkyo belt ~70 smoothed, Shin-Maebashi and Sosha ~63, the central-east (Chuo-Maebashi / Joto / Mitsumata) ~65, Maebashi-Oshima and the south ~50, and the Ogo / Kasukawa fringe ~35–45. Official residential land prices were flat in 2026 (+0.1% 公示地価), with centre commercial points up 2–4% and the Akagi-foothill fringe down 1–1.5% — a flat, bifurcating market.
